claim: MCP has three server-side primitives (tools, resources, prompts), three client-side primitives (sampling, elicitation, logging), lifecycle management via capability negotiation, and a notifications system for real-time updates.
quote: MCP defines three core primitives that servers can expose: Tools: Executable functions that AI applications can invoke to perform actions; Resources: Data sources that provide contextual information; Prompts: Reusable templates that help structure interactions

claim: Streamable HTTP replaced the SSE transport in the Nov 2025 spec; OAuth 2.1 with CIMD and Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) is the current auth model; MCP governance moved to Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in Dec 2025.
quote: With CIMD, a client's identity is a URL pointing to a JSON document the client controls. Authorization servers fetch metadata on demand rather than maintaining a registration database for every client.

claim: Resources are application-controlled context (files, schemas); Prompts are user-invoked server-curated templates; Sampling enables nested LLM calls inside MCP server features.
quote: MCP Prompts allow servers to provide structured messages and instructions for interacting with language models that are catered to the use case.

claim: The three client-side primitives (sampling, elicitation, roots) unlock genuinely new patterns that server-side tools alone cannot provide; sampling fits intent classification and data extraction; sampling fails for real-time voice (200–800ms latency).
quote: The right side, what clients expose to servers, is what unlocks genuinely new patterns that server tools alone can't.

claim: Elicitation pauses server execution to collect structured user consent via a client-rendered form; it should never request passwords or API keys; three outcomes: accept, decline, cancel.
quote: When a potentially destructive action is triggered, the server pauses execution and calls ctx.elicit() with a schema defining required fields. The client renders a native confirmation dialog, ensuring explicit user consent before proceeding.

claim: VS Code (GitHub Copilot) is the only major client with full sampling and elicitation support as of mid-2026; Claude Desktop and Claude Code support neither; servers must check clientCapabilities at runtime.
quote: VS Code (GitHub Copilot) has the most complete implementation supporting both features. Claude Desktop and Claude Code do not yet support either.

claim: Roots are client-declared URIs that scope server operations; they are informational rather than strictly enforced but enable cleaner resolution logic and modular context graphs.
quote: A Root in MCP is a URI that represents a location the client wants the server to pay attention to.

claim: The filesystem MCP server replaces its allowed-directories list entirely with client-provided roots; dynamic roots/list_changed notifications allow scope updates without reconnecting.
quote: Roots notified by Client to Server completely replace any server-side Allowed directories when provided.

claim: Four MCP tool design patterns: workflow-based (bundle multi-step goals), semantic search (vector similarity over large catalogs), code mode (single execute_code tool replacing 50+ calls), and progressive discovery (staged schema exposure).
quote: One CRM case replaced 50+ sequential calls consuming 200K+ tokens with a single code execution tool.

claim: Seven ranked MCP anti-patterns: no audit gates (96), auth after build (90), god-tools (82), schema over-fit (74), missing error discrimination (62), chatty protocols (54), omnibus params blob (46).
quote: A god-tool with an under-specified schema and no audit gate is the modal production failure mode in 2026.

claim: Tool poisoning embeds adversarial instructions in the tool description field; the LLM treats the manifest as authoritative and silently executes injected directives alongside legitimate behavior; the Rug Pull variant exploits lack of version-locking.
quote: The server returns a tool manifest with adversarial instructions embedded in the description field... The model treats the tool manifest as authoritative instructions and follows embedded directives as part of normal reasoning.

claim: A 2026 disclosure exposed approximately 200,000 vulnerable MCP instances across IDEs, internal tools, and cloud services.
quote: A 2026 disclosure exposed up to 200,000 vulnerable MCP instances across IDEs, internal tools, and cloud services.

claim: The MCPTox benchmark tested 45 live MCP servers with 353 authentic tools; popular agents showed tool-poisoning attack success rates above 60%, with the highest at 72%.
quote: Testing 45 live MCP servers and 353 authentic tools, with many popular agents exhibiting attack success rates above 60%, with the highest at 72%.

claim: MCP Tasks (SEP-1686) implement a five-state machine (working, input_required, completed, failed, cancelled); task IDs are capability tokens scoped to the authorization context; tasks/result is a blocking call returning the same payload as the synchronous equivalent.
quote: Once a task reaches a terminal state, it must never move again, ensuring clients don't observe backward transitions during retries or network races.

claim: The 2026 MCP roadmap prioritises stateless Streamable HTTP (removing Mcp-Session-Id), MCP Server Cards for capability discovery without live connections, Tasks lifecycle refinements, and enterprise extensions for audit trails and SSO.
quote: stateful sessions fight with load balancers, horizontal scaling requires workarounds, and there's no standard way for a registry or crawler to learn what a server does without connecting to it

claim: Running Streamable HTTP at scale has surfaced production gaps; the 2026 roadmap addresses sticky session requirements and horizontal scaling constraints.
quote: MCP now runs in production at companies large and small, powers agent workflows, and is shaped by a growing community through Working Groups, Spec Enhancement Proposals (SEPs), and a formal governance process.

claim: MCP Inspector is the official interactive debugger for MCP servers, enabling inspection of raw JSON-RPC messages and testing of all primitive types.
quote: MCP Development Tools for developing MCP servers and clients, including the MCP Inspector

claim: The official MCP reference server repository contains canonical implementations for filesystem, git, GitHub, Slack, Postgres, and memory servers.
The MCP protocol specification repository hosts all Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs) as GitHub issues; tracking open proposals reveals upcoming spec changes before they ship.
quote: MCP Specification: A specification of MCP that outlines the implementation requirements for clients and servers.
